title: By the Sea
checkpoint: Phase 5 (School readiness) — new sound 'ea' (the /ee/ sound as in sea, meal and read)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'ea' — another way to write the /ee/ sound your child knows from 'keep', used in sea, meal and beach. Take care: ea can also say /e/ in some words, but not in this book.

pages.text: Pip and Ned went to the sea.
pages.illustration: Pip and Ned arriving at the top of a dune with the whole sea opening up in front of them. Big sky, big water, two small figures. The reveal page.
Ned's orange feet in clear shallow water at the shoreline, seen close and from above, small waves breaking over them. Cool greens and blues.
Ned working through an enormous picnic — a wrapped sandwich bigger than his head — with total commitment. Comic appetite.
Pip with a small cup of tea balanced on a flat rock, one wing round it, very civilised. Steam rising. Gentle contrast with the previous page.
The two of them sitting side by side on the sand looking out to sea, backs to the reader, small against the horizon. Quiet and companionable.
Ned lying on his front reading a book propped in the sand, feet swinging in the air behind him. Utterly absorbed.
A crab scuttling sideways out of the sand with one claw raised; Ned already airborne in retreat, book flying. Peak comedy.

pages.text: It was a good day out.
pages.illustration: Wide beach scene at golden hour, long shadows, the tide coming in over their footprints. Warm and nostalgic.

pages.text: Pip and Ned had a treat.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the pair walking back up the dune at sunset, sandy, tired, Ned still holding the book. Sea glowing orange behind them.
